purpose: Staged summaries for source review; no production import

candidates.statement: The council plan page reports adoption of Variation No. 1 on 13 July 2026.
candidates.limitation: The variation's substantive effects have not yet been reviewed.

candidates.statement: The May 2024 catchment summary says it uses data up to 2021.
candidates.limitation: Do not present its assessments as live 2026 measurements.

candidates.statement: Uisce Éireann describes a €6.7 million Tagoat wastewater network upgrade.
candidates.limitation: Reported project investment is not verified expenditure or a county investment budget.

candidates.statement: The planned network connection runs to Kilrane and onward through existing infrastructure to Rosslare wastewater treatment.
candidates.limitation: This describes planned dependency, not independently verified operational capacity.

candidates.statement: The project page gives spring 2027 as the expected completion period.
candidates.limitation: Forecast only; do not manufacture a day or mark completed.

candidates.statement: The port describes a €350 million planned investment package spanning several initiatives.
candidates.limitation: Separate masterplan, digitisation, border facilities, road and offshore-renewables components; funding, approvals and delivery require individual review.

candidates.statement: The OPW Feasibility Report (cited in the SFRA) records four major floods in Enniscorthy town in the 20th century, in 1924, 1947, 1965 and 2000; the 1965 flood was the largest, producing levels about 1.25 m higher upstream of Enniscorthy Bridge and about 0.9 m higher downstream of Seamus Rafter Bridge than the November 2000 event.
candidates.sourceLocator: SFRA §2.3.2 (citing OPW Feasibility Report on the Enniscorthy Flooding Problem)
candidates.limitation: Feasibility Report seen only via the SFRA quotation, not retrieved directly. Relative level differences are report figures, not independently verified against a gauge datum.

candidates.statement: The November 2000 fluvial flood of the River Slaney caused considerable damage in Enniscorthy, with many properties over one metre deep in water; flooding resulted from waters exiting the river upstream and moving overland. Single flood events were recorded at St. John's Bridge and Carley's Bridge in November 2000 from the River Urrin.
candidates.limitation: No absolute peak level from an official gauge is stated for this event; depth described qualitatively ('over one metre deep'). floodmaps.ie '12 recorded events' figure is an April 2013 snapshot.

candidates.statement: Met Éireann publishes daily and monthly rainfall for the Enniscorthy-Brownswood station, Co. Wexford, for the period 1983-01-01 to present, under CC BY 4.0.
candidates.limitation: Covers the November 2000 event but NOT the 1924, 1947 or 1965 events. Specific Nov 2000 daily totals not yet extracted. CC BY 4.0 attribution (five Met Éireann statements) required on any reuse.

candidates.statement: OPW operates hydrometric station 12002 Enniscorthy on the River Slaney (Hydrometric Area 12), publishing water level and flow; processed/archival series and Annual Maxima are available via Hydro-Data.
candidates.eventDateText: real-time 5-week rolling window; archive via Hydro-Data
candidates.limitation: Real-time values are provisional/raw/unchecked (5-week window). Whether the 12002 record extends back to November 2000 is not yet confirmed. Reuse under the Irish PSI licence; station-details dataset is CC BY 4.0.

candidates.statement: The Enniscorthy Flood Relief Scheme (public exhibition 2019, submitted 2020) was refused consent in 2022 under Section 7E(1)(b) of the Arterial Drainage Acts as amended by the EU (EIA)(Arterial Drainage) Regulations 2019; the scheme is being progressed on a phased basis and cites extreme floods in 1924, 1947, 1965, 2000 and 2015.
candidates.limitation: Scheme-site statement; exact refusal date within 2022 and full decision reasoning not read from the primary decision document. No reuse licence stated on the site.
